points.title: 童年与少年时期
points.description: 托马斯·曼1875年出生于德国吕贝克的一个富裕商人家庭。父亲是谷物商人，母亲来自巴西的葡萄牙裔家庭。1881年父亲去世后，家庭迁往慕尼黑。这段经历深刻影响了他的创作，尤其是《布登勃洛克一家》中对吕贝克资产阶级生活的描绘。少年时期，他表现出对文学和音乐的浓厚兴趣，但也经历了身份认同的困惑，在艺术与商业之间徘徊。
points.descriptionEn: Thomas Mann was born in 1875 in Lübeck, Germany, into a wealthy merchant family. His father was a grain merchant and his mother was of Brazilian-Portuguese descent. After his father's death in 1881, the family moved to Munich. This period deeply influenced his writing, particularly his depiction of bourgeois life in Lübeck in 'Buddenbrooks'. During his youth, he showed a strong interest in literature and music but also experienced identity confusion, torn between artistic and commercial paths.

points.title: 文学起步与婚姻
points.description: 1894年，托马斯·曼发表处女作《倒下》。1898年出版短篇小说集《矮个子弗里德先生》，获得初步成功。1901年，他的代表作《布登勃洛克一家》出版，这部描写吕贝克资产阶级家族衰落的小说使他一举成名。1905年，他与卡蒂娅·普林斯结婚，这段婚姻持续终生，育有六个子女。在慕尼黑期间，他与艺术家、作家圈子交往密切，形成了独特的文学风格，将现实主义与象征主义相结合。
points.descriptionEn: In 1894, Thomas Mann published his debut work 'Fallen'. In 1898, he released the short story collection 'Little Herr Friedemann', achieving initial success. His masterpiece 'Buddenbrooks' was published in 1901, depicting the decline of a bourgeois family in Lübeck and bringing him immediate fame. In 1905, he married Katia Pringsheim, a marriage that lasted until his death and produced six children. During his time in Munich, he mingled with circles of artists and writers, developing a unique literary style that combined realism with symbolism.

points.title: 创作巅峰期
points.description: 这一时期是托马斯·曼创作的黄金时代。他创作了《威尼斯之死》(1912)、《魔山》(1924)等代表作，探索了疾病、死亡、时间等主题。1929年，他因《布登勃勃洛克一家》获得诺贝尔文学奖。他积极参与魏玛共和国的文化生活，同时保持对政治的谨慎态度。1920年代，他开始公开表达对民主制度的支持，反对极端主义。这一时期，他的作品从个人叙事转向更广阔的社会和政治思考，奠定了他在世界文学中的重要地位。
points.descriptionEn: This period marked Thomas Mann's golden age of creativity. He wrote masterpieces like 'Death in Venice' (1912) and 'The Magic Mountain' (1924), exploring themes of illness, death, and time. In 1929, he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature for 'Buddenbrooks'. He actively participated in the cultural life of the Weimar Republic while maintaining a cautious attitude toward politics. In the 1920s, he began to openly express his support for democracy and opposition to extremism. During this time, his work shifted from personal narrative to broader social and political thinking, establishing his important position in world literature.

points.title: 流亡初期
points.description: 1933年希特勒上台后，托马斯·曼因其公开反对纳粹的立场被剥夺德国国籍。他首先流亡到瑞士苏黎世，在那里发表了著名的反纳粹演讲《论德意志共和国》。在苏黎世期间，他完成了《约瑟夫和他的兄弟们》四部曲的第一部分，并开始创作《浮士德博士》。这一时期，他成为德国流亡知识分子的精神领袖，通过广播演讲和文章向德国国内抵抗运动传递希望和勇气，同时也努力维护德国文化的尊严。
points.descriptionEn: After Hitler came to power in 1933, Thomas Mann was stripped of his German citizenship due to his open opposition to the Nazi regime. He first went into exile in Zurich, Switzerland, where he delivered his famous anti-Nazi speech 'On the German Republic'. During his time in Zurich, he completed the first part of his tetralogy 'Joseph and His Brothers' and began working on 'Doctor Faustus'. This period saw him become a spiritual leader for German exiled intellectuals, conveying hope and courage to the domestic resistance through radio speeches and articles, while also striving to preserve the dignity of German culture.

points.title: 美国流亡
points.description: 1938年，托马斯·曼移居美国，受聘于普林斯顿大学担任客座教授。在美国期间，他完成了《约瑟夫和他的兄弟们》四部曲，并创作了《浮士德博士》和《绿蒂在魏玛》等重要作品。他积极参与反法西斯活动，通过美国广播向德国民众发表讲话。1942年，他成为美国公民。然而，他对美国大众文化的保留态度以及与一些左翼知识分子的分歧，使他在美国知识界也面临一定争议。这一时期，他的作品更加关注欧洲文化危机与艺术家的责任。
points.descriptionEn: In 1938, Thomas Mann moved to the United States and accepted a visiting professorship at Princeton University. During his American years, he completed the 'Joseph and His Brothers' tetralogy and wrote important works like 'Doctor Faustus' and 'Lotte in Weimar'. He actively participated in anti-fascist activities and addressed the German people through American radio broadcasts. In 1942, he became a U.S. citizen. However, his reserved attitude toward American mass culture and disagreements with some left-wing intellectuals caused certain controversies within American intellectual circles. During this period, his works focused more on the European cultural crisis and the responsibility of artists.

points.title: 晚年与回归欧洲
points.titleEn: Later Years and Return to Europe
points.description: 1944年，托马斯·曼移居瑞士帕耶讷，后定居苏黎世。1945年二战结束后，他拒绝返回德国，批评东西德分裂，呼吁德国统一。1952年，他移居瑞士基尔希贝格，1955年在苏黎世逝世。晚年，他完成了《浮士德博士》和《选定的集子》，并发表了《关于我自己》的自传。这一时期，他被尊为欧洲文化传统的守护者，其作品被翻译成多种语言，影响遍及全球。他的晚年思想更加关注欧洲一体化和文化传承，对后世欧洲知识分子产生深远影响。
points.descriptionEn: In 1944, Thomas Mann moved to Switzerland, first to Pully and later to Zurich. After World War II ended in 1945, he refused to return to Germany, criticizing the division of Germany and calling for reunification. In 1952, he moved to Kilchberg, Switzerland, where he died in Zurich in 1955. In his later years, he completed 'Doctor Faustus' and 'The Selected Stories', and published his autobiography 'The Story of a Novel'. During this period, he was revered as a guardian of the European cultural tradition, and his works were translated into multiple languages, influencing people worldwide. His later thoughts focused more on European integration and cultural heritage, having a profound impact on later European intellectuals.

appraisal.zh: 托马斯·曼通常被列为20世纪最伟大的德语作家之一，其作品以精湛手法把个人命运与时代变迁交织，流亡经历和对民主的坚定立场使他成为知识分子的道德典范，对德国文化的批判性继承也为战后文化重建提供了资源。也有研究者指出，他的作品带有明显的精英主义倾向，过于强调艺术与生活的对立，复杂的句法与象征使大众难以接近，早期对魏玛共和国的保留和对美国大众文化的批评则显出文化保守主义。
appraisal.en: Thomas Mann is generally ranked among the greatest German writers of the twentieth century, weaving personal destiny with historical change through masterful technique; his exile and firm commitment to democracy made him a moral exemplar for intellectuals, and his critical inheritance of German culture offered resources for post-war reconstruction. Yet some researchers note a clear elitist tendency, an overemphasis on the opposition between art and life, and complex syntax and symbolism that keep general readers at a distance, while his early reserve toward the Weimar Republic and criticism of American mass culture betray cultural conservatism.

supporter.zh: 托马斯·曼被赞誉为20世纪最伟大的德语作家之一，他的作品深刻探索了人类精神世界的复杂性。支持者认为他通过精湛的艺术手法，将个人命运与时代变迁紧密结合，创造了不朽的文学经典。他的流亡经历和对民主制度的坚定立场，使他成为知识分子的道德典范。托马斯·曼对德国文化的深刻理解与批判性继承，为战后德国的文化重建提供了重要思想资源，其人文主义精神至今仍具有强烈的现实意义。
supporter.en: Thomas Mann is celebrated as one of the greatest German writers of the 20th century, whose works profoundly explore the complexities of the human spirit. Supporters argue that through masterful artistic techniques, he intricately wove personal destiny with historical change, creating timeless literary classics. His exile experience and unwavering commitment to democracy established him as a moral exemplar for intellectuals. Mann's profound understanding and critical inheritance of German culture provided vital intellectual resources for post-war cultural reconstruction in Germany, and his humanistic spirit remains highly relevant today.

critic.zh: 批评者指出托马斯·曼的作品存在明显的精英主义倾向，过于强调艺术与生活的对立，有时显得脱离普通民众。他的政治立场也曾受到质疑，早期对魏玛共和国的保留态度，以及流亡期间对美国大众文化的批评，被认为显示出某种文化保守主义。此外，他复杂的句子结构和象征手法使作品难以被大众接受，被批评为'象牙塔中的知识分子'。一些评论家还认为，他对德国传统的矛盾态度—既批判又眷恋—反映了一种知识分子的无力感。
critic.en: Critics point out that Thomas Mann's work exhibits clear elitist tendencies, overemphasizing the opposition between art and life, sometimes appearing detached from ordinary people. His political stance has also been questioned, including his reserved attitude toward the Weimar Republic in his early years and his criticism of American mass culture during exile, seen as manifestations of cultural conservatism. Additionally, his complex sentence structures and symbolic devices make his works inaccessible to the general public, criticized as an 'intellectual in the ivory tower'. Some commentators argue that his contradictory attitude toward German tradition—both critical and nostalgic—reflects a sense of intellectual powerlessness.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，托马斯·曼被定义为一位连接传统与现代、艺术与政治的桥梁人物。他的作品被广泛研究，特别是《魔山》和《浮士德博士》成为文学分析的经典案例。作为诺贝尔文学奖得主，他的国际影响力超越了德语文学圈。在流行文化中，他的形象与'流亡知识分子'和'文化守护者'紧密相连，成为20世纪欧洲文化危机的见证者。他的生平和作品被多次改编为电影和戏剧，持续影响着当代对知识分子角色和艺术责任的思考。
objective.en: In historical and popular culture, Thomas Mann is defined as a bridge figure connecting tradition with modernity and art with politics. His works are widely studied, with 'The Magic Mountain' and 'Doctor Faustus' becoming classic cases in literary analysis. As a Nobel Prize laureate, his international influence extends beyond German literature. In popular culture, his image is closely associated with 'exiled intellectual' and 'cultural guardian,' becoming a witness to the European cultural crisis of the 20th century. His life and works have been adapted into films and plays multiple times, continuing to influence contemporary thinking on the role of intellectuals and the responsibility of art.

self.zh: 艺术家是人类的良心，他必须说出真相，即使真相是痛苦的。
self.en: The artist is the conscience of humanity, he must speak the truth, even if the truth is painful.
